Requested splits:
- Neha: complete the security/provenance tab (checksums, artifact locations, attestations, SOC2 references). Add where we provide reproducible artifacts vs. third-party vendor provenance.
- Rishi: draft the model update policy section — version pinning options for dedicated vs hosted, notification cadence, rollback SLA, rollback tooling (canary, pin/unpin APIs).

Quick notes on version handling I discussed with Product: our standard is to serve a pinned model version per route unless customers opt into auto-updates; for hosted tier we offer notification feeds and a 14-day optional auto-update window; for Dedicated/Private we always respect customer pinning and provide signed release notes. We should enumerate how we sign/verify binaries and provide checksums for each release.

Please reply in-thread with your ETA and any blockers.

Folks —

I've filled the provenance/security tab and attached the Helix_RFI_answers.xlsx. Highlights:

- Provenance artifacts: for Redwood-curated models we provide origin manifests including source model repo, commit hash, build container digest, and model file SHA256. For third-party models we provide the upstream source pointer and any available SBOM-like exports; we clearly mark limitations when upstream provenance is partial.
- License traceability: produced a CSV (redwood_rfi-appendix_license_map.csv) mapping model artifacts to license types (Apache-2.0, MIT, GPL-compat indicators) and any license exceptions. We also note runtime dependencies that can impact license obligations.
- Version pinning & updates: recommended defaults included in Rishi's section; from a compliance perspective we never auto-upgrade pinned environments without explicit opt-in; notifications and signed release notes are provided for all hosted updates.
- Evidence: included sample checksum proof (signed manifest examples) and a link to our internal attestations repo; for customers requiring deeper evidence we can grant time-limited access to an artifacts bucket under an NDA.

Kenji —

Thanks for your patience. Attached is our completed response package: Helix_RFI_answers.xlsx and an appendix mapping licenses and dependency traces (redwood_rfi-appendix_license_map.csv). Key takeaways up front:

- Provenance & artifacts: For Redwood-curated models we supply signed manifests (commit hashes, container digests, model file SHA256) and reproducible build instructions where applicable. For vendor-upstream models we provide upstream pointers and note any provenance gaps.
- License traceability: We map each model artifact to its license and highlight any obligations affecting redistribution or derivative works.
- Version pinning & updates: By default, routes are pinned to a model_rev identifier. Customers choosing auto-updates receive signed release notes and a 14-day preview window before auto-apply (hosted); Dedicated/Private always respect explicit pinning. Rollback support and canary policies are documented.
